title: Word list safety: no email or cloud copies; checking the list without typing it
plain:
The recovery word list (the seed phrase, usually 12 or 24 words on paper or card) is the master key to the inherited bitcoin. Anyone who sees those words can move the coins, so every place you put a copy is a security decision.

Should you send the words to yourself by email, or save them online, so they survive a house fire? No — never store the seed phrase online or in the cloud. An email copy is a permanent leak anyone can read later: mail servers keep copies, accounts get broken into, and whoever reads those words owns the bitcoin.

For the fire worry, the rule is physical offline copies only; metal survives fire. A stamped metal plate, kept somewhere secure in a location separate from the paper original, protects against fire and flood without creating any digital copy.

If any app or website asks you to confirm the word list by typing it in, that is not a safe check. Count the words on paper instead — 24 or 12 is what a complete list looks like. Also check that every word is readable and the order is unchanged.

Never type the seed words anywhere except verified wallet software at recovery time — official wallet software you downloaded yourself, used only when you are actually restoring the wallet. This app never asks for your words. If a website, caller, or 'helper' asks you to type or read the words out, stop: it is a theft attempt.
technical:
BIP-39 seed phrases (12 or 24 words) encode the wallet's master private key, so possession equals control of the funds. Any digital transcription — email, cloud storage, notes apps, password managers, photos, screenshots — creates a durable, searchable copy that may outlive the account holder and is a leading vector for post-inheritance theft. Fire and flood resilience is achieved offline: stamped or engraved metal plates stored securely, in a location separate from the paper original.

Completeness is verified on the physical medium only: confirm the word count (24 or 12), legibility, and order. Entering seed words is legitimate only during an actual recovery, in verified wallet software obtained from the vendor's official channel on a trusted device. This app never requests, transmits, or stores seed words; no legitimate service asks for a seed phrase to 'verify' it.

claims.claim: No — never store the seed phrase online or in the cloud.
An email copy is a permanent leak anyone can read later.
Use physical offline copies only; metal survives fire.
Count the words on paper instead — 24 or 12 confirms a complete list.
Never type the seed words anywhere except verified wallet software at recovery time.
This app never asks for your words.

warnings: Never email, photograph, screenshot, or upload the seed words anywhere — including notes apps, cloud drives, or password managers.
Anyone or anything asking you to type, paste, or read out seed words is attempting theft; stop immediately.
Do not reset or wipe an inherited hardware wallet before its recovery backup is located and verified.
Keep paper and metal copies in separate secure locations so one disaster cannot destroy every copy.
